A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Physics-Informed Diffusion Models by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison; v2 Appendices A–H correspond to v3 Sections A.1–A.8.

before.justification: v2 reports original Darcy-flow and topology-optimization experiments, plus unit-circle experiments comparing training objectives and residual-estimation methods.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds topology-optimization baseline results and a unit-circle loss-weight sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the PIDM loss, equation 13 in v2 and equation 14 in v3, retain the same training procedure, residual weighting, and mean or two-pass DDIM estimation. The architectures and extensions for inequality constraints and optimization objectives are unchanged. New baseline adaptations do not change PIDM itself.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the unit-circle toy problem, Darcy permeability/pressure fields, and topology optimization with in- and out-of-distribution boundary conditions. The Gaussian-prior toy variant already appears in v2. The added weight sweep uses the existing task and does not introduce new data or environmental conditions.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds PG-Diffusion and CoCoGen to the topology-optimization comparison, alongside the retained Diffusion, TopoDiff-G, and DOM baselines. These two methods previously participated only in the Darcy comparison. This is a limited extension of comparator membership within an existing benchmark.

E3.justification: v3 Figure 7 introduces evaluation of 400 generated samples at each of six residual weights: 0, 0.005, 0.02, 0.04, 1, and 5. Appendix A.6.3 specifies equilibrium and volume residuals for the added topology baselines and a constant CoCoGen scaling selected by median residual on the in-distribution test set. Existing splits, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6.1 and new Figure 7 systematically test how residual weighting affects constraint error and sample diversity. v2 already compared four loss/prior configurations and discussed collapse under excessive residual weighting, but lacked this six-setting sensitivity analysis. The existing ablations and out-of-distribution evaluations are retained.

E5.justification: Figures 5–6 retain the same reporting of 10 training runs with different seeds and 25th/75th-percentile bands. Figure 2 retains averages and individual residuals for 16 samples every 10,000 iterations. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical estimation procedures are specified for the added results.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark scores and sample figures are unchanged. New Table 1 rows report in-/out-of-distribution residuals of 1.82e-3/1.92e-3 for PG-Diffusion and 1.51e-3/1.56e-3 for CoCoGen, plus compliance and volume errors. Figure 7 adds residual values from 0.080 at c=0 to 0.0024 at c=5, accompanied by lost diversity. These are additional results, not improvements to previously reported PIDM scores.

T1.justification: The consistency proposition and proof, score-based estimation, likelihood-ratio approximation, DDIM derivation, and auxiliary-objective mathematics are retained. The newly displayed residual-vector equation in Section 2.2 restates v2's concatenation of PDE and boundary-condition residuals rather than introducing a new mathematical construction.

C1.justification: The abstract makes the outperformance claim benchmark-specific, including up to two orders of magnitude lower flow residuals. The introduction explicitly positions PIDM as filling a missing first-principles framework unifying diffusion models and PINNs, extending v2's presentation of constraint-informed training and synergies. The principal regularization, inference-speed, and constraint-generality claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds an interpretation of the residual objective as sampling from an unnormalized target and distinguishes this from data-free sampling. Section 3.3 adds a temperature/annealing analogy. The sensitivity discussion also gives more specific guidance on balancing diversity and residual minimization; the existing fixed-grid limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.6.3 documents the added baselines' residual components and explains that CoCoGen's full Jacobian exceeds available GPU memory, motivating constant scaling and a parameter search. v3 also explicitly supplies the toy residual formula and Darcy residual assembly. The architecture and training tables, hardware, runtimes, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds connections to data-free sampling through Zhang and Chen's Path Integral Sampler, Vargas et al., and Berner et al., and to annealed combinatorial optimization through Sanokowski et al. The first-principles novelty positioning becomes more explicit, while most related-work discussion remains. Publication and title updates for retained references are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, portions of the introduction, and Darcy-results discussion are rewritten, with added explanations of coordinates, residuals, and clean-signal estimates. Citations become author–year references, and Appendices A–H become subsections A.1–A.8. The main section sequence and most technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the six-panel sensitivity Figure 7, expands and resizes Table 1, and reformats the hyperparameter tables. Retained figures are relocated or regrouped, and the document adopts ICLR title, heading, and running-header styling. Earlier Figures 7–8 remain as Figures 8–9 with the same sample content.

improvement.justification: The added topology baselines broaden the comparative evidence, while Figure 7 directly demonstrates the residual–diversity tradeoff that v2 discussed largely qualitatively. Clearer residual definitions and baseline implementation details also improve interpretability. These are limited gains: the core method, proof, and retained results are unchanged, and the new CoCoGen comparison applies to the disclosed constant-scaling adaptation rather than an exact reproduction.
